newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Greens call for censure of EU Commission over BSE.
newsitem.headline: Greens call for censure of EU Commission over BSE.

text.p: Greens in the European Parliament called on Friday for the European Commission to be censured over its handling of the mad cow disease crisis if it did not change its ways.

Citing a draft report from a parliament committee of inquiry, the Greens said in a statement that the Commission had mismanged the situation, failing to provide adequate controls against bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).
"The Commission...has given completion of the internal market, which took place at the same time as the BSE crisis, priority over public health," Euro-MP Johannes Voggenhuber said in the statement.
But the political group stopped short of demanding an immediate censure vote, saying the current Commission should be given until the end of the year to make changes in its procedures and personnel.

A draft report on the BSE crisis, which came to a head last year when the Commission imposed a worldwide ban on British beef exports, criticises the European Union executive for delaying the release of data on BSE. It said this helped to undermine public confidence and worsen the economic damage.
It did not recommend any sanctions againt the Commission.

The report also said the British government had failed to enforce properly a ban on animal-feed exports containing meat and bone meal. It had pressed the European Commission to avoid inspecting British slaughterhouses between 1990-94 and failed to take adequate heed of scientific warnings.
Commission officials have been unwilling to comment on the report, saying it may yet be amended. But the Commission has in the past denied allegations of mismanagement.
Euro-MPs are expected to discuss the report, which follows a four-month investigation by a 19-member cross-party committee of inquiry at a plenary session in Strasbourg, France, in February.
Commission President Jacques Santer is due to address the committee of inquiring next Wednesday during the parliament's January Strasbourg session.
